findings.title: Meeting coffee machine is a featureless near-black cube with its cup modelled inside the body, and it sits on top of the desk keyboard
findings.problem: The Meeting has a bonus, "leave the coffee machine alone", and a sneaky route whose prompt is "Borrow the coffee machine's cable". Both depend on the player recognising the coffee machine, but the prefab doesn't read as one. It is a 0.55 m rounded INK cube (`rbox(w,h,d)` in `m=toon(INK)`) with one red 0.2×0.1 block on the front. The cup is a `cyl(.06,.05,.1)` at z .12, which is inside the 0.275 m half-depth body, so it is never visible. The low-angle shot `props-gallery-31-low-row.jpg` shows only the cube and the red button. There is no spout, drip tray, water tank, bean hopper or display. Under ACES the body renders at a median rgb(8,4,21), luma about 6, in `props-gallery-24-meeting-coffee-close-o250.jpg`. That breaks the DR-54 rule that the darkest tone is ink-blue and never black. The outline is the same colour as the body, so the silhouette disappears against shadows. From the back (`props-gallery-10-sheet05`, coffee back) it is a plain black box. It also sits on the default desk at (-14,5) with y 1.3, right on top of the desk's own keyboard from `deskClutter`, which pokes out from under the machine (`props-gallery-24b-crop-coffee-on-keyboard.jpg`). At the game camera (`props-gallery-22-meeting-coffee-gamecam.jpg`) it reads as a black speaker or bin. The steam puff above it is the only clue.
findings.fix:
Rebuild `case 'coffee'` in src/props/prefabs.ts:108 as an espresso machine in DMETAL and cream (for example a body of `#dcdfe6` with an INK front panel), not solid INK:
- Body: `rbox(w,h*.78,d*.8,.06)` at y `h*.11`, z `-d*.1`.
- Overhang head: `rbox(w*.9,.12,d,.05)` at y `h/2-.06`.
- Spout: `cyl(.03,.02,.08)` under the head at z `d*.3`.
- Drip tray: `rbox(w*.7,.03,d*.3,.015)` in METAL at y `bottom+.02`, z `d*.32`.
- Cup: move it out to z `d*.32` so it stands on the drip tray, with a cream `cyl(.05,.045,.09)` plus a torus handle.
- Water tank: a translucent `toon('#8fd0f0',{opacity:.7})` box on the back at z `-d*.4`.
- Keep the red button, plus a small `lit()` power LED.

Then fix the desk underneath. Either give the coffee desk at src/levels/meeting.ts:28 a variant with no keyboard (add a `variant` that skips the keyboard and mouse in `deskClutter`, for example `v===5`), or move the machine to x -14.4 so it sits over the pencil-cup side.
findings.verify: Rerun `node mockups/review5/tools/props-gallery/shoot.mjs` with `only=coffee` (front and back), and retake `props-gallery-22`, `-24` and `-24b` through `mockups/review5/tools/props-gallery/meeting.mjs`. The cup and drip tray should be visible at the game camera, the body median luma should be ≥ 40, and no keyboard should show under the machine.
findings.verify_reason: The code matches the finding. At src/props/prefabs.ts:108 the coffee machine is rbox(w,h,d) in INK (prefabs.ts:16) plus a red 0.2 m block. The cup is cyl(.06,…) at z .12, so it spans z .06–.18, inside the 0.275 m half-depth body, and is never visible. meeting.ts:28 places the machine on a default desk (variant 0), whose deskClutter always draws the keyboard (prefabs.ts:42). The keyboard edge pokes out under the machine in props-gallery-24b and in my own shot. Under ?norim the body's median pixel is rgb(0,0,18), luma about 2, so it renders effectively black and breaks DR-54. At the game camera it is an unmarked black box; only the steam puff (game.ts:443-444) and the 'Borrow the coffee machine's cable' prompt identify it. P1 is borderline, because that prompt names it when you are near the reel. I kept P1 because the bonus 'Leave the coffee machine alone' (objectives.ts:39) depends on recognising the object.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-props-gallery-01-meeting-coffee-zoom9-norim.jpg: black cube on the coffee desk, keyboard edge visible under it; median body pixel rgb(0,0,18) measured with PIL
src/ui/objectives.ts:39 and :82 (bonus text and prompt that name the machine)
findings.fix_correction: The desk-variant part needs both edits. In deskClutter (prefabs.ts:42), skip the keyboard and mouse when v===5. In meeting.ts:28, give the coffee desk `variant:5`; it currently has no variant, so it defaults to 0. Moving the machine to x -14.4 would put it over the v0 pencil cup (local x -.55) instead, so prefer the variant. The rest of the fix is fine.

findings.title: Job yellow is the default colour of decorative props: yellow mugs on all 32 Meeting desks, yellow beanbags, yellow desk lamps, and yellow clutter beside the Lunch wedge
findings.problem:
DR-45 reserves job yellow (`#ffc94d`/`#ffc629`) for job items. Several decorative prefabs default to it anyway:
- **Mug:** defaults to `#ffc94d` (prefabs.ts:12). The Meeting desk loop spawns mugs with no colour (meeting.ts:16), so every one of the 32 desks carries a job-yellow mug, visible in `props-gallery-20b-crop-meeting-yellow-mugs.jpg`.
- **Beanbag:** defaults to `#ffc94d` (prefabs.ts:26). The Meeting lounge places a yellow one at (10,4.6) right next to Pip's spawn path; it is the same yellow as Pip's hat and the job reel (`props-gallery-29-meeting-lounge-close.jpg`).
- **Desk lamp:** the `deskClutter` lamp picks from `['#e5484d','#3f7fd6','#ffc94d','#6cc58a']` (prefabs.ts:47), so a quarter of the desk lamps are job yellow.
- **Clutter palettes:** these feed every recipe, including boxes, carts, chairs, reels and cabinets:
  - garage `#ffc629`: yellow carts, chairs, boxes and a yellow cabinet stack (`props-gallery-51c-garage-close-o300.jpg`, `-51b`);
  - lunch `#ffc94d`: yellow boxes on the cart next to the yellow doorstop wedge (`props-gallery-52c-lunch-close-o300.jpg`) and in the corridor beside the yellow cable bridges (`-52b`);
  - arcade `#ffd84d` and observatory/spectrum `#ffd66b`, both within about 10 ΔE.

The player learns that yellow means a job part (reel, strip, wedge, splitter, bridge, plug). Dozens of yellow decoys dilute that cue and send the grab prompt to junk (DR-17, DR-43). This is related to the known RESEARCH_ART F4, but the default prefab colours (mug and beanbag) and the Meeting hand placements are separate root causes that F4's per-kind palette fix alone does not touch.
findings.fix:
1. In src/props/prefabs.ts, change the mug default to a non-job hue such as `#fffaf0` (white) or `#e5484d`, and the beanbag default to `#e5484d`.
2. In `deskClutter` (prefabs.ts:47), replace `#ffc94d` with `#b392f0`, or a desaturated `#e0b47a`.
3. In src/levels/meeting.ts:29, recolour the lounge beanbags to non-job, non-BLOBC fabric, for example `#e5484d` and `#3f7fd6`.
4. Remove `#ffc629`, `#ffc94d`, `#ffd84d` and `#ffd66b` from the clutter `colors` arrays in garage.ts:31, lunch.ts:18, arcade.ts:29, observatory.ts:25 and spectrum.ts:34. Alternatively, filter them out in clutter.ts with a ΔE > 25 test against `#ffc94d` before `pick(r,c)` at clutter.ts:75.
5. Add a unit test: for every level, `clutter()` output plus hand-placed props whose kind is not in `{reel,strip,wedge,splitter,bridge,plug,supply,coupler}` and has no id has no colour within 25 ΔE of `#ffc94d`.
findings.verify: Add the unit test in tests/ (for example `props-palette.spec.ts`), then retake `props-gallery-20`, `-29`, `-51c` and `-52c`. The only yellow things in each start and survey shot should be job items.
findings.verify_reason: The code matches. The mug default is '#ffc94d' (prefabs.ts:12) and the beanbag default is '#ffc94d' (prefabs.ts:26). meeting.ts:16 spawns 32 mugs with no colour (8 pods × 4 desks). meeting.ts:29 sets the beanbag to color:'#ffc94d'. The desk-lamp palette includes '#ffc94d' (prefabs.ts:47). Job yellows appear in the clutter colour lists: garage '#ffc629' (garage.ts:31), lunch '#ffc94d' (lunch.ts:18), arcade '#ffd84d', observatory and spectrum '#ffd66b'. The screenshots show it: yellow mugs on every Meeting desk (20b); the yellow beanbag (29); in the garage, yellow cabinet, cart and chair (51c); in Lunch, a yellow box on the cart (52c). In the Lunch survey (52b), yellow boxes sit near the yellow wedge, the mop and the yellow bridges. That directly breaks DR-45's check. One small error: the lounge beanbag at (10,4.6) is not 'next to Pip's spawn path'; the Meeting spawn is (-10,-5.8) (meeting.ts:33). Another yellow source the finding missed: the bookshelf `books` palette also contains '#ffc94d' (prefabs.ts:52).
findings.fix_correction: Also remove '#ffc94d' from the `books` array at prefabs.ts:52, and from the pencil colours at prefabs.ts:45. The finding suggests replacing the desk-lamp yellow with '#b392f0'. That is acceptable for a thin lamp, but '#b392f0' is BLOBC[0], so never reuse it on rounded props.

findings.title: Beanbag still reads as a bun or macaron: brown bread in Playground, pastel macarons in Arcade and Observatory, and exact coworker hues in Meeting and Lobby
findings.problem:
This confirms RESEARCH_ART F5 and REVIEW5 P5 against the current build; it is still open. The model is still two even lobes: a squashed sphere `(1,.48,1)` plus a back sphere `(1.12,.72,.78)`, a thin seam torus and a faint dent (prefabs.ts:130-137). From the game camera:
- Playground: the kraft `FLOOR` colour (no palette passed) makes it a brown bread loaf or bun (`props-gallery-42-playground-lounge-gamecam.jpg`, `-61-playground-pins-close.png`).
- Arcade: pink, mint, yellow and lilac versions are macarons (`props-gallery-50c-arcade-close-o300.jpg`).
- Observatory: the same (`props-gallery-54c-observatory-close-o300.jpg`).
- Gallery close-up: a flat yellow bun (`props-gallery-10-sheet11-plug-wedge-beanbag.jpg`).

DR-52 is also broken directly by hand placements:
- Meeting puts a `#5b9cf0` beanbag at (14.6,4.4); that is exactly BLOBC[2], the coworker blue (meeting.ts:29, kit.ts:10).
- Lobby uses `#b392f0`, which is BLOBC[0] (lobby.ts:7).
- Arcade's `#9b7bf0` and `#6fe0c0` are within a few ΔE of BLOBC lilac and mint.

A rounded pastel lump in a blob hue next to rounded pastel blob coworkers muddies the "who is a person" read. Players see buns and macarons, not seats.
findings.fix:
Implement the F5 fix in src/props/prefabs.ts:130-137:
- **Body:** one `T.LatheGeometry` teardrop (bottom r .45, waist .40 at y .25, top .22 at y .55), tilted back 0.35 rad about x.
- **Seat dent:** a darker flattened sphere `.24`, scale `(1,.15,.9)`, at y .32 on the front.
- **Top:** a pinched cone tuft at the top.
- **Seams:** 3 seam tori down the back.
- **Variety:** a ±0.08 rad lean taken from `variant`.

Colour:
- Replace `#5b9cf0` in meeting.ts:29 with `#3f7fd6` or `#e5484d`.
- Replace `#b392f0` in lobby.ts:7 with `#f08a4b`.
- In clutter.ts, filter the beanbag colour so it is more than 15 ΔE from every BLOBC entry, and never use `FLOOR` kraft for it (use `CHAIRC` minus the job yellow).
findings.verify: Shoot `only=beanbag` at yaw -.5 and 2.64 with `shoot.mjs`, then retake `props-gallery-42`, `-50c`, `-54c` and `-29`. Show a first-time viewer a flat-filled `?norim` crop: it should be named "beanbag" or "sack seat", not bun, macaron or blob.
findings.verify_reason: prefabs.ts:130-137 is still two squashed spheres plus a seam torus. Playground passes no `colors` (playground.ts:5), so it gets FLOOR kraft. My own Playground shots show brown bun or bread lumps (verify-props-gallery-04, -05), and the gallery sheet11 shows a yellow bun. meeting.ts:29 uses '#5b9cf0', which is exactly BLOBC[2] (kit.ts:10). lobby.ts:7 uses '#b392f0', which is BLOBC[0]. In the Arcade (50c) and the Observatory (54c), pastel pink, mint, lilac and yellow lumps sit beside blob coworkers. This breaks DR-52 as written.
extra_evidence: src/render/kit.ts:9-10 (CHAIRC and BLOBC share three hues)
findings.fix_correction: Part of the colour fix breaks the rule it is meant to fix. '#f08a4b', proposed for lobby.ts:7, is BLOBC[3]. 'CHAIRC minus the job yellow' still contains '#b392f0', '#6cc58a' and '#f08a4b', which are BLOBC[0], [1] and [3] (kit.ts:9-10). Use only non-blob fabric hues such as '#e5484d', '#3f7fd6' or a desaturated '#7a6a8f'. Filter them in clutter.ts by ΔE > 15 against every BLOBC entry, not against CHAIRC.

findings.title: Coupler is the player's own plug model recoloured teal, so the coupler-before-reel order can't be read from its shape
findings.problem: `case 'coupler':case 'plug':` (prefabs.ts:101-102) builds both kinds from the same geometry: a tapered cylinder with two brass prongs. game.ts:86 builds the cable end Pip carries as `makeProp('coupler','#ffcc52')`. So the Meeting's coupler at (-3.6,4.7) is literally Pip's yellow plug painted teal (`props-gallery-10-sheet04-bin-reel-coupler.jpg`, `props-gallery-32-pip-scale-handhelds.jpg`). The Meeting rule is that the coupler must go on before the second reel. R4B and the checklist item M8 asked for that order to show in the shape of the parts (DR-37). Today a player sees two identical plugs and nothing says which end mates where. Only a failed try, the wobble plus the badge, teaches it. The two shapes are also hard to tell apart in hand, and the coupler's teal is outside the job-item visual language (DR-45). The prongs also stick out of the box collider by 9 cm on the coupler and 12 cm on the plug (measured with `mockups/review5/tools/props-gallery/measure.mjs`), so they clip into walls and sockets.
findings.verify: Run `shoot.mjs` with `only=coupler,plug`, then a blind-play shot at the Meeting mail cart (walk to (-3.6,4) and zoom to 9). A viewer should be able to say "the plug goes into the coupler" without having failed first. `tests/routes.spec.ts` coupler-order tests still pass.
findings.verify_reason:
The shared geometry is real. `case 'coupler':case 'plug':` builds both from one model (prefabs.ts:101-102), and Pip's carried cable end is makeProp('coupler','#ffcc52') (game.ts:86). The prong overhang is correct by arithmetic: prongs end at x .27, against a coupler half-width of .18 and a plug half-width of .15. However, the claim that 'only a failed try teaches the order' is wrong:
- With the plug in hand near the reel, the prompt says 'Attach the coupler first' before any try (objectives.ts:77).
- The attach code sorts the coupler ahead of the reel whenever both are within 1.9 m (game.ts:233). The coupler sits only 0.6 m from the reel on the cart, so pressing F at the cart normally attaches it first automatically.
- The extension and coupler are not in the Meeting's required steps (objectives.ts:31-35); they are optional extra cable.
The 'plug' kind is never placed as a physics prop in any level, so the plug's 12 cm prong overhang has no gameplay effect. That makes this P2. New evidence: the teal coupler (#56d2c6) sits on the teal-blue mail-cart tray (#5f8fa8) and nearly disappears there (verify-props-gallery-02, -03).
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:233 (the coupler is preferred when both parts are in reach)
src/ui/objectives.ts:31-35 (Meeting steps do not require the coupler or extension)
mockups/review5/shots/verify-props-gallery-03-meeting-mailcart-coupler-o300.jpg (teal coupler on the teal cart edge)
findings.fix_correction: If the 'coupler' case is rebuilt as an adaptor, game.ts:86 must change to makeProp('plug','#ffcc52'). Otherwise Pip's carried cable end turns into the new adaptor model. Recolouring the coupler to job yellow is also the fix for it blending into the teal cart tray. Keep it within DR-45, with ink stripes.

findings.title: Clutter colour families still break: pink, mint and purple cardboard, yellow and teal cabinets and shelves, kraft beanbags
findings.room: arcade, garage, qfn, observatory, spectrum, playground
findings.problem:
This confirms RESEARCH_ART F4 is still open at HEAD. `clutter()` uses one `colors` list for every kind in a recipe (clutter.ts:61 and :75 `pick(r,c)`), so:
- Arcade cardboard boxes are pink `#ff7eb6` and mint `#6fe0c0` (`props-gallery-50c-arcade-close-o300.jpg`, `-50b-arcade-survey.png`).
- Garage cabinets, carts and chairs are job yellow and teal (`-51b`, `-51c`).
- QFN shelves and cabinets are mint `#7fe6c6`, and its boxes lavender `#c7b8ff` (`props-gallery-53c-qfn-close-o300.jpg`).
- Observatory boxes are dark purple `#4a4380` and beanbags lilac (`-54c`).
- Spectrum boxes are red, pink and yellow gift blocks (`-55b`).
- Playground beanbags are kraft brown, i.e. bread (`-42`).

Cardboard that isn't kraft and shelves that are teal stop reading as office things. At 26 m the floor turns to confetti and job parts don't pop (DR-51, DR-53, DR-69). The beanbag and job-yellow aspects are filed separately; this finding covers the per-kind family system.
findings.fix:
Make `ClutterOptions.colors` a `Partial<Record<PropKind,string[]>>`, keeping `string[]` as an accent fallback, and resolve colours per kind inside `RECIPES` (clutter.ts:33-52):

| Kind | Colours |
|---|---|
| `box` | always `FLOOR` kraft; the level accent goes on the box label card only (add a label colour via `variant`, prefabs.ts:61) |
| `cabinet` | `['#aab3c2','#dcdfe6','#f4efe6']` |
| `bookshelf` | `[METAL,'#b98552']` |
| `cart` | `['#5f8fa8','#9aa3b2']` |
| `chair`, `beanbag` | level accents with BLOBC and job-yellow hues filtered out |
| `mug` | accents |
| `reel` (parts) | grey `#c7ccd6` flange, so it isn't a job reel |

The arcade keeps its pastel identity in the floor, cabinets, rugs and marquees.
findings.verify: Add a unit test that runs `clutter()` with each level's options in a stub world and asserts every box colour is in `FLOOR`, every cabinet is office-neutral, and no beanbag is within 15 ΔE of BLOBC. Retake the `props-gallery-5xb` survey shots.
findings.verify_reason:
clutter.ts:61 and :75 pass one `colors` list into every recipe, and each recipe colours boxes, cabinets, carts, shelves, mugs, beanbags and reels with pick(r,c) (clutter.ts:34-49). The level lists match the finding: arcade '#ff7eb6' and '#6fe0c0'; qfn '#c7b8ff' and '#7fe6c6'; observatory '#4a4380'; spectrum '#b0406a' and '#ffd66b'; playground none, so FLOOR. The screenshots I looked at show it:
- QFN: mint cabinets and a mint box, lavender boxes (53c).
- Arcade: pink and mint cardboard boxes (50c).
- Observatory: a dark-purple box and lilac beanbags (54c).
- Garage: a yellow cabinet, cart and chair (51c).
- Spectrum: red, pink and yellow boxes (55b).
This breaks DR-51's 'no pink or teal boxes, no teal shelves'.
extra_evidence: src/levels/clutter.ts:34-49 (every recipe calls pick(r,c) for unrelated kinds)
findings.fix_correction: Same caveat as finding 2: the chair and beanbag accent filter must exclude every BLOBC hue, not just job yellow. CHAIRC itself contains three BLOBC hues.

findings.title: Every prop gets a cuboid collider: round props rest on invisible corners, reels and bins can't roll, and hollow furniture is a solid block
findings.problem:
`addProp` always creates `ColliderDesc.cuboid(size/2)` (game.ts:124), and `clearOfFixtures` uses `RAPIER.Cuboid` too (clutter.ts:67). That causes three problems.

**(a) Round props in box colliders.** Beanbag 0.9 m sack, plant pot, bin, mug, cone, reel and lamp base all sit in boxes. A tipped bin or plant rests on box corners that aren't there, and a reel, which begs to be rolled in a cable game, slides like a crate. This breaks R12.3/DR-71's "round props have round colliders".

**(b) Hollow furniture is solid.**
- The desk's 1.6×0.95×0.85 box fills the leg room. Chairs can't tuck in, and a thrown mug bounces off air at the desk edge.
- The ping-pong table's 2.6×0.9×1.5 box fills the space under the table.
- The mop bucket is 0.5 m tall inside a 1.5 m box, so a metre of invisible wall stands above it.
- The lamp's 0.65×1.5 box surrounds a thin pole.
- The wedge's full box makes its slope non-physical.

See the magenta wireframes in `props-gallery-10-sheet01`, `-07`, `-08` and `-09`.

**(c) Visual parts poke out of the collider by more than 3 cm** (R12.3), measured with `mockups/review5/tools/props-gallery/measure.mjs`:

| Prop | Part | Outside the collider |
|---|---|---|
| cart | handle | +29.5 cm up, 14 cm out |
| coolbox | lid handle | +19 cm |
| printer | paper tray | 17 cm out of the front |
| ping-pong | net | +16 cm |
| whiteboard | feet | 15 cm each side |
| dolly, supply, capcart | handles | 14.2 cm |
| plug / coupler | prongs | 12 / 9 cm |
| chair | back | +10.4 cm |
| plant | foliage | 6.5 cm |
| splitter | outlets | 6 cm |

These parts clip through walls and through anything stacked on top. Going the other way, the printer top sits 6 cm below its collider and the lamp shade 8 cm below, so things set on them float.
findings.fix:
1. Add an optional `collider` field to `Prefab` (prefabs.ts:7): `{shape:'cyl'|'ball'|'compound',parts?:...}`.
2. In game.ts:124, build the matching shape:
   - **Cylinders:** `ColliderDesc.cylinder(h/2,r)` for bin (r .19), mug (.07), plant (pot r .26 plus a ball for the foliage), cone (.22), and reel (axis z, r .34, as a cylinder rotated by the collider's rotation).
   - **Round cuboid:** `ColliderDesc.roundCuboid` (radius .1) for the beanbag.
   - **Compound:** multiple colliders on the same body for the desk (top slab plus two leg panels), ping-pong (top plus 4 legs), mop (bucket cylinder r .27 h .5 plus a thin handle capsule), lamp (base cylinder plus pole capsule plus shade cylinder), wedge (`ColliderDesc.convexHull` of the 6 wedge vertices), chair (seat box plus back box plus base cylinder) and whiteboard (board plus two foot bars).
3. Shrink the visuals that poke out:
   - printer tray depth `d*.2`;
   - coolbox handle torus r .09, raised lid inside the box;
   - handles of cart, dolly, supply and capcart drawn at x `-w/2+.05` instead of `-w/2`;
   - chair prefab height .95 → 1.06.
4. Mirror the shapes in clutter's `clearOfFixtures`.
findings.verify: Extend `drive.audit()` (or the review measure script) to report any mesh more than 3 cm outside its collider. Expect none. Run `npm.cmd test` routes and layout specs. Throw a bin and a reel in the Playground: they roll.
findings.verify_reason:
game.ts:124 always uses ColliderDesc.cuboid, and clutter.ts:67 uses RAPIER.Cuboid. DR-71 explicitly requires round colliders for beanbag, plant, bin and cone. I checked the overhang figures against prefabs.ts:
- cart handle: tube to h/2+.25 plus r .04, so +29.5 cm; x −.1−.04, so 14 cm out.
- coolbox handle: +19 cm.
- printer paper tray: z .375 + .169, so 16.9 cm out.
- ping-pong net: +16 cm.
- whiteboard feet: half of d*2.5 is .25 against half-depth .1, so 15 cm.
- chair back: about +10 cm.
- printer top: ends 6 cm below the collider top.
All match the finding. One correction: the 'plug' kind is never spawned as a physics prop (grep of src/levels), so its prong overhang has no effect in game.
extra_evidence: kit.ts:113 (handle tube reaches y1 plus radius .04, at x−.1)
mockups/review5/shots/props-gallery-10-sheet06-printer-whiteboard-bookshelf.jpg (the printer tray pokes out of the magenta box)
findings.fix_correction: Rapier's `ColliderDesc.cylinder` is y-axis, so the reel needs `.setRotation()` with a quarter turn about x to put its axis on z. A chair collider change of .95 to 1.06 also shifts the spawn height (game.ts:121 uses size[1]/2), so re-run the layout and audit after it. Drop the plug from the overhang list unless 'plug' props get placed.

findings.title: Start-of-level interpenetrations from hand-placed and recipe y and offset values (cabinet+box ×23, monitor+paper ×32, lounge paper inside a beanbag ×11, reel inside the mail cart)
findings.room: meeting, garage, qfn, playground, arcade, observatory
findings.problem:
Running `g.audit(.02)` on every level (`mockups/review5/tools/props-gallery/probe2.mjs` and `probe3.mjs`) gives Meeting 51 overlaps, Arcade 6, Playground 3, QFN 3, Garage 2 and Observatory 1, against DR-70's target of zero. Root causes:

**Cabinet + box (18 in Meeting, 2 in Garage, 3 in QFN).**
- meeting.ts:21 puts a box at y 1.9 on a cabinet whose top is 1.625 (centre .825 + .8). The box bottom is then 1.6, sunk 2.5 cm.
- clutter.ts:47's `cabinets` recipe has the same y 1.9.

**Monitor + paper (32 in Meeting).** meeting.ts:16 places paper at x−.38, inside the 0.63 m monitor collider footprint (monitor at z±.17, bottom at y .96 vs paper at y .99).

**Beanbag + paper (lounge recipe; 3 Playground, 6 Arcade, 1 Observatory).** clutter.ts:38 puts the paper at (.1,.65), within the second beanbag's 0.45 half-width at (.55,.15).

**Mail cart + extension reel (1).** meeting.ts:27 puts the reel at y 1, 3 cm into the cart.

On the first physics steps the solver pushes these apart. Boxes jitter or pop off the cabinets, and paper squirts out from under monitors, producing start-of-level motion and possible damage-free noise.
findings.fix:
- Cabinet box: in meeting.ts:21 and clutter.ts:47, set the box y to `1.95` (cabinet top 1.625 + box half 0.3 + .025).
- Monitor paper: in meeting.ts:16, move the first paper to x `x-.55` (clear of the monitor footprint), or drop it below the monitor's z band (`z+out*.3`).
- Lounge paper: in clutter.ts:38, move the paper to `{dx:0,dz:.95}` or `{dx:-1.15,dz:.4}`.
- Extension reel: in meeting.ts:27, set y `1.03`.

Add `expect(await drive.audit(.02)).toEqual([])` for every level to the layout spec.
findings.verify_reason:
I reproduced it exactly with my own audit script (mockups/review5/tools/verify-props-gallery/audit.mjs, g.audit(.02)):

| Level | Overlaps | Pairs |
|---|---|---|
| Meeting | 51 | monitor+paper 32, box+cabinet 18, extension+mail-cart 1 |
| Playground | 3 | beanbag+paper |
| Arcade | 6 | beanbag+paper |
| Garage | 2 | box+cabinet |
| QFN | 3 | box+cabinet |
| Observatory | 1 | beanbag+paper |
| Lunch | 0 | — |
| Spectrum | 0 | — |

The causes are confirmed by arithmetic:
- Cabinet top is 1.625 and the box bottom is 1.6.
- The paper at x−.38 (span −.53..−.23) overlaps the monitor's x ±.315 and the monitor's z band by 3 cm, and its y .975 is below the monitor bottom .96 + …
- The lounge paper at (.1,.65) overlaps the second beanbag's footprint.
- The cart top is .675 and the reel bottom is .65.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-props-gallery/audit.mjs (output: meeting 51, playground 3, arcade 6, garage 2, qfn 3, observatory 1, lunch 0, spectrum 0)
findings.fix_correction: Moving the monitor paper to x−.55 puts it on top of deskClutter's visual items: pencil cup −.55, photo frame −.6, pen cup −.62, paper stack −.5 (prefabs.ts:43-46). Prefer moving it along z away from the monitor, to z+out*.08. The monitor is at z−out*.17 with a half-depth of .085, and the paper's half-depth is .115, so this leaves about 4.5 cm of clearance.

findings.title: Bookshelf books are still uniform candy bricks, saturated and poking above the frame
findings.problem: This confirms RESEARCH_ART F10 is still open. Each shelf holds 7 identical `box(.14,.34,d*.7)` books, 14 cm thick (about 3× a real book), in full `CHAIRC`-style saturated colours (prefabs.ts:52, :123-125). The top row reaches y .97 against a frame top of .9, so the books stick 7 cm out of the frame and the collider. There is no back panel or top. The gallery (`props-gallery-10-sheet06`) and the Meeting lounge (`props-gallery-29c-meeting-lounge-close-low-o500.jpg`) show crayon or brick blocks, the most saturated thing in frame, competing with the cable (DR-53). The R7 cues are missing: 10–14 thin spines of varied height, one leaning, one gap, desaturated colours. The colour wrap formula itself is fixed; no undefined colours appear (re-check item).
findings.fix:
Per F10, in prefabs.ts:123-125:
- 11–13 books per shelf from a seeded loop: width `.05+.04*rand`, height `.22+.12*rand` (cap .3 so the top row ends below .9), depth `d*.75`.
- Leave one gap of .12, and lean one book `rotation.z=.25`.
- Add a darker spine band `box(w*1.01,.03,.01)` at 70% height.
- Desaturate `books` by 25% (for example `#c77a7c,#6f93c4,#86b99a,#d9bf7a,#a796c9,#93bfb8`).
- Add a back panel `box(w,h,.02)` in METAL at z `-d/2+.01` and a top board.
- Merge the books into one geometry per shelf variant to keep draw calls down.
findings.verify: Run `shoot.mjs` with `only=bookshelf`, and retake `props-gallery-29c`. The book top must stay ≤ the frame top in `measure.mjs` (`over+` y ≤ 0).
findings.verify_reason: prefabs.ts:125 draws 7 books per shelf, box(.14,.34,…) at y+.2. The top row ends at .6+.2+.17 = .97, against post tops at h/2 = .9, so the books stand 7 cm proud. The `books` palette is fully saturated (prefabs.ts:52) and includes job yellow. In sheet06, QFN (53c) and Observatory (54c), the books are uniform candy blocks poking over the frame. There is no back panel.

findings.title: Vending machine is still a red slab with a sticker grid and a blank back
findings.problem: This confirms RESEARCH_ART F14 is still open. The prefab is `rbox(w,h,d)` plus a pale window box plus 9 coloured 0.14 m squares (prefabs.ts:126-128). It has no header band, coin and button panel, dispense flap or glass shelves. In the Meeting (`props-gallery-24-meeting-coffee-close-o250.jpg`) it reads as a red cupboard with sticky notes. The back and sides are flat red faces of up to 2×1 m, against DR-62's 0.5 m² limit (`props-gallery-25-meeting-vending-back-o700.jpg`, `props-gallery-10-sheet07`). The re-check item "Lunch vending machine faces +z" passes: it is decor (`decor.ts`), and the window faces the camera in `props-gallery-52b-lunch-survey.jpg`.
findings.fix:
In prefabs.ts `case 'vending'`:
- **Front:** a header band `rbox(w*.9,.22,.05)` in a lighter shade plus a glyph decal at y `h/2-.18`. Make the window `box(w*.62,h*.55,.04)` toon `#bfeaf5` opacity .6, with 3 METAL shelf strips `box(w*.6,.02,.06)`. Put the goods (cans `cyl(.05,.05,.12)`) behind the glass, not on it.
- **Side panel:** at x `w*.36`, an INK `rbox(.18,.5,.04)` with a coin slot and 6 small cream buttons.
- **Dispense flap:** INK `rbox(w*.5,.18,.04)` at y `-h/2+.25`.
- **Back:** a vent decal and 2 panel seams.
findings.verify: Run `shoot.mjs` with `only=vending` at yaw -.5 and 2.64, and retake `props-gallery-24` and `-25`. Every face over 0.5 m² should carry a trim or a decal.
findings.verify_reason: prefabs.ts:126-128 is rbox, a pale window, and 9 squares at d/2+.03, which sit on the glass surface rather than behind it. In sheet07 the back is a fully blank red 1.0×2.0 m face (2 m²), and the side faces are 0.8×2 m. That breaks DR-62's 0.5 m² limit. In props-gallery-24 it reads as a red cupboard with sticky notes.

findings.title: Large office props have bare single-colour backs: cabinet, printer, cooler, monitor and coffee machine
findings.problem:
DR-63 asks for a finished back because the camera orbits. From yaw 2.64 (`props-gallery-10-sheet*`, the back column):

| Prop | Back |
|---|---|
| cabinet | one 0.7×1.6 m grey face, 1.1 m², no seams (prefabs.ts:87-92) |
| printer | plain white box, with the INK top slab and nothing else |
| water cooler | plain cream body |
| monitor | an INK slab; a stand post shows but no rear housing bump or ports |
| coffee machine | plain black (prefabs.ts:108) |

Cabinets stand back to back in rows in the Meeting and in clutter (`cabinets` recipe), so these backs are often in view when orbiting. They read as cardboard stage flats.
findings.fix:
- **Cabinet:** 3 horizontal seam strips `box(w*.9,.015,.01)` in the dark shade on the back face at the drawer lines, plus a small cream inventory sticker `box(.12,.08,.01)`.
- **Printer:** a rear vent panel (a `rbox(w*.5,.18,.02)` in DMETAL) and an INK power-socket square; on the front, add a control panel strip `rbox(.25,.04,.1)` in INK with a `lit()` LED on top at the front-right.
- **Cooler:** an INK back vent grid (`box(.3,.4,.01)` decal) and a cord stub.
- **Monitor:** a rear housing bump `rbox(w*.5,h*.4,.04)` in INK at z `-.08`, and an off-white logo dot.

Keep these parts merged per kind so they batch.
findings.verify: Rerun the back views with `shoot.mjs` (yaw 2.64) for cabinet, printer, cooler and monitor. No single-colour face over 0.5 m² remains.
findings.verify_reason:
The back views in sheet02, sheet03, sheet06 and sheet07 show untrimmed backs on the cabinet (0.7×1.6 m, about 1.1 m²) and the printer (about 0.85×0.85 m, about 0.72 m²). Both break DR-62. Two corrections:
- **Backs under 0.5 m².** The monitor back (about 0.24 m²), the cooler back (about 0.48 m²) and the coffee machine back (about 0.36 m²) are below DR-62's 0.5 m² limit. They are DR-63 'finished back' polish only, not DR-62 breaks.
- **Meeting cabinets.** The claim that cabinets 'stand back to back in rows in the Meeting' is wrong. The Meeting's 18 cabinets are a single row at z −9.2 with their backs against the north wall (meeting.ts:21, depth 20), so those backs are never visible. The clutter `cabinets` recipe places two cabinets side by side (clutter.ts:47) with a random quarter turn, so it is only there that backs can face the floor.
findings.fix_correction: Prioritise the cabinet and printer backs, which are real DR-62 breaks, and clutter-placed cabinets. The monitor, cooler and coffee machine backs are lower-priority DR-63 polish.

findings.title: Water cooler, printer and ping-pong table miss their identifying cues at the game camera
findings.problem:
DR-62 wants 2–4 cues per prop.

**Water cooler** (prefabs.ts:129): a cream block plus a translucent cylinder that renders as a grey drum. It has no taps (hot and cold), drip tray or cup dispenser (`props-gallery-10-sheet07`, `props-gallery-22-meeting-coffee-gamecam.jpg`). It reads as a bin or paper-towel tower.

**Printer** (prefabs.ts:118): a white cube plus a black top and a thin paper slab that pokes 17 cm out of the collider. No output tray lip, control panel or paper stack. At the game camera (`props-gallery-26-meeting-printer-strip-close.jpg`) it is a white bin. That matters because the first Meeting step says "Fetch the power strip by the printer".

**Ping-pong** (prefabs.ts:140-142): a green slab with a net. No white edge or centre lines, paddles or ball; legs are INK sticks (`props-gallery-10-sheet07`).
evidence: src/ui/objectives.ts (Meeting step 1 text references the printer)
findings.verify: Run `shoot.mjs` with `only=cooler,printer,pingpong`, then retake `props-gallery-22` and `-26`. A viewer names "water cooler" and "printer" from the game-camera crop.
findings.verify_reason:
The code confirms the missing cues:
- **Cooler** (prefabs.ts:129): a block plus a translucent drum, with no taps or tray.
- **Printer** (prefabs.ts:118): a body, an INK slab and a paper slab that sticks out about 17 cm.
- **Ping-pong** (prefabs.ts:140-142): a slab, a net and INK legs, with no lines, paddles or ball.

Sheet06 and sheet07 show the same. Whether these props are named correctly is subjective. The cooler's drum-on-block still roughly reads as a water cooler in props-gallery-22 and verify-01. The printer in props-gallery-26 reads as a white box with a black lid. The strip it identifies is marked by the objective arrow and the 'Grab the power strip' prompt, so this is polish (P2).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-props-gallery-01-meeting-coffee-zoom9-norim.jpg (the cooler at left reads as a cooler-ish drum on a block)

findings.title: Cable bridge and doorstop wedge are sharp, bare yellow extrusions with no functional cues
findings.problem:
Both are job items in Lunch Rush, built with `ExtrudeGeometry({bevelEnabled:false})` (prefabs.ts:143-145 and :177-182). This is the known R5.2 / DR-58 break, still open.

The **bridge** is a 1.8×1.0 m flat-shaded yellow trapezoid with a black top strip (`props-gallery-10-sheet08`). It has no cable channels on its underside or ends, no ramp ribs and no hazard stripes. Nothing says "cables pass under me safely", which is the concept it stands in for (the water short in Lunch, DR-33/DR-37). Its 24-triangle mesh renders as hard flat facets, unlike every other rounded prop.

The **wedge** ribs are fine, but its edges are razor sharp and it lacks the ink stripes of the job-item language (DR-45) (`props-gallery-32-pip-scale-handhelds.jpg`).
findings.verify: Run `shoot.mjs` with `only=bridge,wedge` at yaw -.5 and 2.64, and retake the Lunch survey `props-gallery-52b`. The bridge's channels read at zoom 9, and lit chamfers show on every edge.
findings.verify_reason: Both extrusions use bevelEnabled:false (prefabs.ts:144 and :178). DR-58 explicitly requires bevelled extrusions. In sheet11 and the gallery the wedge has razor edges, and the bridge is a flat yellow trapezoid with a black strip (sheet08, the Lunch survey 52b).
findings.fix_correction: With ExtrudeGeometry the bevel grows the shape outward by bevelSize, and grows the depth by bevelThickness on both caps. To keep the collider size, inset the shape by bevelSize (.02) and also set `depth: d - 2*bevelThickness` (d−.04). Then translate z by −(d−.04)/2 −.02 rather than −d/2.

findings.title: Playground bowling "pins" are white traffic cones on square plates: low contrast on the pale floor, with a stepped collar
findings.problem: The six Playground pins are `cone` props recoloured `#fffaf0` (playground.ts:18). Pins are the room's designed chaos bonus ("knock down all six pins") and the slingshot's reward target (DR-06, DR-10), but the model reads as white traffic cones: a square 0.5 m base plate plus a cone. The cone's reflective band is a separate `cyl(.12,.15,.1)` that is wider than the cone at that height, so it shows as a stepped collar (prefabs.ts:139, `props-gallery-10-sheet12-cone-strip.jpg`). On white the band vanishes. White on the about-200-luma Playground floor gives very little contrast at the game camera (`props-gallery-61-playground-pins-close.jpg`, `-41-playground-survey.png`). The square box collider also means a pin must tip a full 45° about a plate edge to count as down, unlike a real round-based pin.
findings.verify: Run `shoot.mjs` with `only=pin,cone`, and retake `props-gallery-61` and `-41`. The pins should read as bowling pins with ≥ 25 luma contrast against the floor (DR-54 `?norim` check), and the cone shows no step.
findings.verify_reason: playground.ts:18 makes the six pins `cone` props in '#fffaf0'. The cone model is a square 0.5 m plate, a cone, and a band cyl(.12,.15) (prefabs.ts:139). The cone's radius is about .098 at y .11 and about .132 at y .01, so the band sticks out 1.5–2 cm and shows as a step. My own shots (verify-props-gallery-04, -05) show white traffic cones on square plates with that visible collar, not bowling pins. One correction: the contrast claim is overstated. In my full-fx zoom shot the pin's lit side measures luma about 229 against the floor's 195, a 34-luma gap, which passes DR-54's 25-luma threshold in that sample. The tipping claim is also loose: the box tips past its edge at about 39°, and pinsDown also counts a pin displaced by more than 0.5 m (game.ts:252-253).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-props-gallery-05-playground-pins-zoom9.jpg (pin luma 229 vs floor 195, measured with PIL)
findings.fix_correction: Keep the pin model fix. Drop the DR-54 contrast justification, or re-measure it with ?norim on the shadow side before claiming it.

findings.title: Floor lamp is still an unlit mushroom: no bulb, no underside glow, no cord
findings.problem: This confirms RESEARCH_ART F15 is still open. The lamp is still base, pole and a closed `cyl(.18,.32,.34)` shade (prefabs.ts:157-159). At the game camera in the Observatory (`props-gallery-54c-observatory-close-o300.jpg`) the shades are white discs on sticks, repeated many times by the `reading` recipe, which is listed twice in observatory.ts:25. The shade is a closed cylinder, so from below you see a flat cap, not a lit interior. The R7 cues (warm bulb or underside glow, weighted base) are only half there.
findings.verify: Run `shoot.mjs` with `only=lamp`, and retake `props-gallery-54c`. A warm bulb is visible under each shade, and there are fewer lamps.
findings.verify_reason: prefabs.ts:157-159 is an INK base, a pole and a closed cyl shade, with no bulb or cord. In props-gallery-54c the Observatory shows many white shade-on-stick lamps. `reading` appears twice in the recipe list at observatory.ts:25. That repetition is a deliberate weighting, like pod and shelf which are also listed twice, but it does multiply the lamps.

findings.title: Capacitor cart, power strip and reel lack the electrical cues that make them read as what they teach
findings.problem:
Three props that carry the taught concepts are generic.

**capcart** (prefabs.ts:169-172): four plain blue cylinders with grey caps plus an INK box. They read as paint tins or gas bottles (`props-gallery-10-sheet10`). Real electrolytic capacitors show a sleeve with a minus stripe and +/− terminals on top. That is the one visual hint that these store charge and that polarity matters.

**strip** (prefabs.ts:138): the Meeting power strip is an orange bar with 4 sockets and a red switch, but no lead or plug tail. Its 5 A breaker, the load-budget concept, has no visible reset button or rating label, only the red cylinder.

**reel** (prefabs.ts:100 / kit.ts:115-119): a plain white drum with no wound-cable texture and no plug parked on the flange, so it reads as an empty spool.

Per DR-47 the state should be shown on the device itself, and per DR-62 each device needs ≥ 2–4 cues.
findings.verify: Run `shoot.mjs` with `only=capcart,strip,reel`, then the Lunch survey and a Meeting close-up of the strip. The capcart reads as "capacitors" and the strip has a lead.
findings.verify_reason:
The capcart and reel parts are confirmed in code:
- **capcart** (prefabs.ts:169-172): plain blue cylinders with grey caps, and no polarity stripe or terminals. In sheet10 they look like paint tins. It is the Lunch 'capacitor' job item (lunch.ts:5).
- **reel** (prefabs.ts:100, kit.ts:115-119): a plain drum, with no wound-cable texture.

The strip part is largely refuted. Its tripped and overloaded state is already shown in the world by src/meeting-strip.ts:
- a wall load gauge above the strip's spot;
- a separate red reset cap (resetCap);
- a breaker badge.

So the DR-47 argument does not hold for the strip. Missing a lead is cosmetic. 'Read as paint tins' is a subjective naming test I did not run with a viewer.
extra_evidence: src/meeting-strip.ts:1-7, 25, 51-57 (load gauge, reset cap, breaker badge)
findings.fix_correction: Drop the strip's DR-47 claim, because src/meeting-strip.ts:25-57 already provides the gauge, reset cap and badge. Keep the optional lead tail and rating plate as cosmetic polish. The capcart and reel fixes stand.

findings.title: Prop gallery tool hides the coupler behind the vending machine and floats labels away from their props
findings.problem: The review and dev gallery at tools/gallery/index.html lays the 35 prefabs on a 7-wide grid with a fixed camera (gallery.ts:13-15). The 2 m vending machine in row 2 stands directly in front of the 0.36 m coupler in row 1. In `props-gallery-01-tool-gallery-all.jpg` the coupler is invisible, and its label floats on the vending machine's top. The glass pane covers part of the cabinet. It has no back views, no collider overlay and no scale figure, so the gallery can't be used for the DR-59, DR-61, DR-63 or DR-71 checks the rulebook says it serves. A reviewer or artist checking prefabs there will miss small props entirely. Note: tools/ is out of scope for edits in this review. The replacement page used here is at mockups/review5/tools/props-gallery/gal.html.
findings.verify: Open `/tools/gallery/index.html?box=1&pip=1` and confirm all 35 labels sit under visible props, including the coupler and plug. Then `node tools/debug/gallery.mjs`.
findings.verify_reason: tools/gallery/gallery.ts:13-15 lays the props on a fixed 7-column grid with one camera. In props-gallery-01-tool-gallery-all the coupler is hidden behind the vending machine and its label sits on the vending machine. The reel label also lands on the bookshelf, and the glass pane overlaps the cabinet. There are no back views and no collider overlay. Partial mitigation: `?only=` and `?cols=` already let you isolate small props (gallery.ts:2, 7-8). This is a dev tool, not player-facing, so P2.
extra_evidence: tools/gallery/gallery.ts:2 and :7-8 (the only and cols options exist)

notes.models:
I judged all 35 prefabs in src/props/prefabs.ts:
- **Gallery shots:** front and back (yaw −0.5 and 2.64) next to Pip (measured at 1.76 m) and a 1.1 m blob, with magenta collider wireframes, combined into `props-gallery-10-sheet01…12`.
- **Measurements:** I measured each prefab's visual bounds against its collider box (`mockups/review5/tools/props-gallery/measure.mjs`).
- **In-game:** I found the props at the game camera and at zoom 9 in Meeting, Playground, Arcade, Garage, Lunch, QFN, Observatory and Spectrum.

**What works well:**
- Chair: the best prop. Padded seat, curved back, armrests, gas lift, a five-star base on casters. Reads from any angle.
- Box: tape, flap seam and label read well.
- Desk: panel legs and pedestal, with per-desk dressing (keyboard, mouse, pencil cup, desk lamp, cable tail).
- Mail cart: lipped tray with parcels.
- Mop bucket: wringer and bail.
- Splitter: sockets plus a green power lamp.
- Coolbox, cabinet front, dolly reel and supply cart (bolt decal, sockets, handle): all good.
- Materials: every prop uses only `MeshToonMaterial`, with `MeshBasic` for screens and decals, which passes DR-57.
- Scale: Pip-relative scale is on the R6 table. Desk .95, cabinet 1.6, chair seat about .5, supply 1.3; the mug at .16×.2 is in the oversized-handheld range. Every handheld is above 8 px at the game camera.

**Weak:**
- Coffee machine: a black cube with its cup inside it.
- Sofa: floats 12.5 cm and has a one-slab seat.
- Coupler: the same model as the plug.
- Beanbag, books, vending machine, lamp: the known research issues, all still open.
- Water cooler, printer, ping-pong table, bridge, capacitor cart: thin on cues.
- Colliders: every prop is a cuboid regardless of shape.
notes.clarity: The prop silhouettes mostly read at the game camera. Prop colour is what hurts clarity. Job yellow appears on 32 Meeting mugs, a Meeting beanbag, desk lamps, and the Garage and Lunch clutter palette (yellow carts, boxes, chairs and cabinets next to the yellow wedge and bridges). That dilutes the one visual language that marks job parts. The Meeting coffee machine is the target of a bonus and of a prompt ("Borrow the coffee machine's cable"), yet it doesn't read as a coffee machine. The coupler and the player's plug are the same shape, so the coupler-first rule can't be read from the parts.
notes.fun: For a physics-comedy game the props are pleasantly knockable. Boxes scatter when Pip sprints through the Meeting stack, chairs tip, and bins spill paper balls. The chaos bonus targets are weak, though. The Playground "bowling pins" are white traffic cones on square plates, low-contrast on the pale floor. Cuboid reels and bins can't roll, which wastes the most cable-flavoured slapstick props in the game.
notes.teaching:
Props are where the electrical concepts become physical, and several underplay it:
- **Capacitor cart:** reads as paint tins, with no polarity sleeve or terminals.
- **Power strip:** no lead and no breaker or rating plate, even though it carries the Meeting load-budget beat.
- **Reel:** looks like an empty spool.
- **Cable bridge:** shows no cable channel, so it doesn't say "cables pass safely under me".
- **Coupler:** looks like a plug, not a socket adaptor.

Each of these can carry its idea in its shape (DR-37) without any text.
